title.narrative: Public-Private Partnerships and Public Investment Advisory Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to develop a pipeline of feasible private and publicly funded projects.

The objective of the Public-Private Partnerships and Public Investment Advisory Project for Afghanistan is to develop a pipeline of feasible private and publicly funded projects. The project has three components: (1) Strengthening institutional and technical capacity component will strengthen the capacity of relevant institutions and support development of a Public Investment Management - Public-Private Partnerships framework; (2) Infrastructure project preparation facility component will support establishment and operation of an Infrastructure Project Preparation Facility, including development of its governance structure, institutional roles and responsibilities; and (3) Project management component will support the operation of the Project Management Unit to carry out its monitoring, management, and implementation obligations under the project until it is mainstreamed into the Afghan civil service.

title.narrative: Number of feasibility studies completed and approved

comment.narrative:
<p>As part of PPIAP project restructuring in September 2020, the wording of this PDO Indicator was changed from “Number of feasibility studies that lead to tendered projects” to “Number of feasibility studies completed and approved” to clarify the definition of the indicator and to include public investment projects.</p>

<p>
The Bank provided its final no-objection to the feasibility study for FTTX project on April 13, 2021.</p>

comment.narrative:
<p>The intermediate indicator “Number of institutional development recommendations (implemented)” with a baseline of 0 and target of 10 was further defined in April 2019. Ten institutional development recommendations were proposed as follows:</p>

<p>(1). Establishment of PMU and staffing of key PMU positions (2). Establishment of IPPF as a line item in GoIRA annual budget (3). Formal establishment of PEC for PPIAP (4). Formal approval of Terms of Reference for PEC (5). Regular quarterly meetings of PEC for PPIAP held (6). Recording and timely circulation of minutes for all PEC meetings (7). PPIAP sub- projects are in compliance with the PPP Law (8). PPIAP sub-projects are in compliance with latest PIM processes (9). PPIAP fiduciary processes are in compliance with Project Procurement Manual and Project FM Manual (10). PPIAP GRM is implemented a nd has started collecting sub-project level grievances</p>

<p>Recommendations 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 have been fulfilled. Recommendations 7, 8 and 9 had earlier been met but need to be reviewed for compliance in light of the 2020 amendment to the PPP Law and the 2020 PIM Regulations.</p>

title.narrative: Number of GoIRA and CPA staff who are CP3P certified

comment.narrative:
<p>As part of PPIAP project restructuring in September 2020, end target was changed from 150 certifications (Foundation + Preparation + Execution) to 100 Foundation level certifications based on a realistic assessment of the progress and attainable target for this indicator.</p>
<p>The baseline reflects that, as of the Project approval date, 29 GoIRA staff (of which 11 CPA an d 2 women) had successfully completed the CP3P Foundation Certification with financing from the Project Preparation Grant. Since approval, another 21 GoIRA staff (of which 6 women) have successfully completed the CP3P Foundation Certification.</p>

title.narrative: PPP Policy and Regulations operationally applied (implemented)

comment.narrative: <p>The PPP Law was revised (through a process led by the IMF) and approved by the Cabinet on September 5, 2018. The CPA had also drafted the PPP Regulations that were submitted to the Cabinet for approval. In October 2020, the PPP Law was amended and therefore this indicator is not met.</p>
<p>IPPF was established and disbursed funds to the consulting firms EPTISA, EcoConserv, and KMCC.</p>
